The BLOC lineage question is now narrower and more answerable: whether Healing Through Cannabis LLC previously operated as, or acquired, whatever entity used the BLOC brand at the same Urbana address/phone number — that is a rebrand/history question, not an active-license question, since the current license is unambiguous.

services.description:
Cannabis Operator; Dispensary / Retail
Multi-state medical/adult-use dispensary operator, discovered via Pass 2 B2B relationship mapping rather than category research — surfaced no vendor edge itself but was found while researching a Sapphire/VALERE-adjacent facility search and independently confirmed as a genuine directory gap. Two confirmed Ohio locations: Urbana (962 N Main Street) and Lewis Center (8020 Orange Centre Drive), both showing active medical and adult-use sales on first-party location pages. UNCONFIRMED LINEAGE NOTE, flagged rather than asserted: an older BLOC website listed a coming-soon Urbana dispensary at this exact address (962 N Main Street) with this exact phone number (937-910-7744). Same facility and same phone number establish strong operational continuity but do NOT by themselves establish a corporate transaction, rebrand, license transfer, or ownership relationship between BLOC and Feel State — that would need a targeted DCC licensing/lineage check before being written as fact. DCC ROSTER CONFIRMATION (2026-08-16): the licensed legal entity behind both Ohio locations is Healing Through Cannabis LLC — Urbana (962 N. Main Street, CCD000019-00, Active) and Lewis Center (8020 Orange Center Drive, CCD000271-00, Active) are both confirmed current dispensary licenses under this exact name. Neither "Feel State" nor "BLOC" appears anywhere in the DCC roster as a licensed entity name — both are trade names/brands operating under Healing Through Cannabis LLC, not the legal entity itself. This confirms Feel State is a genuine, currently active Ohio operator at both addresses already on file. The BLOC lineage question is now narrower and more answerable: whether Healing Through Cannabis LLC previously operated as, or acquired, whatever entity used the BLOC brand at the same Urbana address/phone number — that is a rebrand/history question, not an active-license question, since the current license is unambiguous.

services.description:
Cannabis Operator
Confirmed via Ohio Cannabis Coalition coverage: Akron-based Klutch (founder Adam Thomarios) is an active Ohio cannabis operator/brand. Documented current brand-partnership relationships, independently corroborated from two separate sources: Klutch's own June 2026 Columbus-opening press release names Cookies, Josh D and Kiva Confections directly as brand partners carried alongside Klutch's house brands (Klutch Cannabis, Citizen by Klutch, Habitat by Klutch); Klutch's Featured Brands page separately confirms the same three and additionally states Josh D has been Klutch's Ohio partner since 2018 ("OG Ohio partner"). None of the three brands are added as directory rows — see this Directory's scope note on national CPG brand-licensing entities. Also documented: an M&A/license-transfer relationship with Farkas Farms (also in this Directory) — DCC approved Klutch's June 2026 acquisition of Farkas Farms' Columbus dispensary license (5429 Bethel Sawmill Center), while Klutch simultaneously sold its Loudonville dispensary/license to Farkas Farms. Confirmed via eight independent sources including Crain's Cleveland Business. Vendor relationships, all current and confirmed via Klutch's own site: CannaPlanners (website/digital development — credited as site provider), Headset (brand-locator/data technology powering the statewide "Find Klutch Near Me" tool — narrow integration, not a broader analytics contract), Dutchie (Dutchie Pay accepted in-store), and CanPay (accepted cashless payment option). CannaPlanners, Headset, Dutchie and CanPay are all also entries in this Directory. Wholesale/distribution relationships into named current Ohio dispensary partners, per Klutch's own statewide locator: Ascend Cannabis, Amplify and Backroad Wellness (all three also entries in this Directory) are explicitly listed as current dispensary partners carrying Klutch products. The same locator names a further 17 already-listed Ohio operators as partners (Curaleaf, Elevated Growth, Ethos, Farkas Farms, Green Leaf Therapy, Greenlight, Guaranteed Dispensary, Locals, Pure Ohio Wellness, Standard Wellness, Story Cannabis, Sunnyside/Cresco, The Botanist, The Cannabist Company, The Forest, Trulieve and Verilife/PharmaCann) — recorded here rather than duplicated across 17 individual rows, since the relationship is the same in each direction (Klutch products carried at these retailers) and is fully documented by this one current source. DCC LEGAL ENTITIES: Klutch's Akron cultivation operates under AT-CPC of Ohio, LLC (CCC000042-00, -01); Bethel Sawmill Columbus under ATCL2, LLC (CCD000218-00); Wellington under related-pattern ATCL4, LLC (CCD000193-00), not independently confirmed as Klutch beyond naming pattern; Cleveland, Northfield and Akron/Tallmadge under Klutch Prospect LLC, Klutch Northfield LLC and Klutch Akron LLC; processing under Klutch Processing LLC (CCP000043-00). Address-level reconciliation now also confirms the Canton and Lorain Klutch storefronts under Citizen Real Estate, LLC / CCD000083-00 and CCD000084-00; both were formerly branded The Citizen by Klutch. SETTLED 2026 OWNERSHIP TRANSFER: On 2026-09-01 Klutch announced DCC approval to acquire Culture Cannabis Club's Grandview dispensary at 1305 Holly Ave, Columbus. Klutch's Grandview dispensary opened on 2026-09-11; the DCC legal entity remains Culture Retail Partners of Ohio, Inc. pending a roster change.

FINAL DISPOSITION: moved out of scope rather than left open indefinitely. This is now the second independent research pass to flag the same problem — a domain-for-sale Contact page (asking $50,000+) alongside leadership bios ("John," "Emma," "Michael," "Sarah," "David," "Karen" — first names only, generic template copy) that no independent source, including Ohio-government or credible organizational records, corroborates. items.name: Ohio Legal Help: record sealing
items.description: Statewide explanation of sealing, expungement and legal-aid options. Start here to identify the right assistance for your county.

items.name: Eligibility interview and action plan
items.description: A guided record-sealing interview that produces next steps. Have your court names, case numbers and charge details ready. This general tool is separate from the marijuana-specific statute below.

items.name: Opportunity Port
items.description: Currently serves Franklin County residents seeking help with Ohio records. Legal assistance is free; filing fees may apply. Services outside Franklin County are paused.

items.name: Marijuana-specific expungement: ORC 2953.321
items.description: Effective March 20, 2026. Covers specified marijuana/hashish possession cases from before that date, including certain dismissed cases. Apply to the sentencing court with case information and evidence of the covered offense. Relief requires a court process; it is not automatic. The statute sets a $50 application fee unless indigent.

resource_routes.title: Start as a medical patient or caregiver

items.name: Ohio patient and caregiver steps
items.description: Official steps for obtaining a recommendation, registering and purchasing medical cannabis. Bring an active registry card, active recommendation and government-issued ID when purchasing.

items.name: Patient registry help
items.description: For registry questions, the state publishes 1-833-464-6627 and MMCPRegistry@com.ohio.gov. Choose patient and caregiver resources on the DCC page.

items.name: Home growing: ORC 3796.04
items.description: Adults 21+ may grow up to six plants per person, with no more than twelve at one residence. Grow at your primary residence in a secured enclosed area, inaccessible to people under 21 and not visible from public space. Rental prohibitions and other residence restrictions apply. The section prohibits selling homegrown marijuana, hydrocarbon extraction and public consumption.

items.name: Ohio cannabis law: current chapter
items.description: Read the current law for possession, transport, purchase, patient and other requirements. Home-growing permission does not answer every possession or transport question.

items.name: State cannabis guidance
items.description: The official hub links the Ohio Cannabis FAQ, current rules and patient guidance. Use current state sources when an older online summary conflicts.
